target_customer: Patients in Chile and Mexico needing lab tests at home, plus health insurers and clinics that partner with it
problem: Getting lab exams in person is slow and costly. Examedi sends nurses and technicians to patients' homes, with online booking and digital results.
business_model: Marketplace and service provider charging per exam, with insurer and clinic partnerships (Clinica Alemana, Isapre alliances)

founders.name: Andres Kemeny
prior_employers: Two startups from a Chilean government backed accelerator (names not given)
education: Left a civil engineering program, no degree
founders.background_notes: YC page. DF reporting says Kemeny later left, completing the departure of the original founders.

founders.name: Juan Pablo Zepeda
education: Industrial engineer, Santiago; left a master's program in optimization
founders.background_notes: YC page: built logistics infrastructure at Houm.

founders.name: Ian Lee
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in Chilean press (DF, Ecosistema Startup); not listed on the YC page. Later left the CEO role; Mariano Werner became CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling, routing and results platform for a field workforce; operations heavier than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Partnerships with clinics and insurers help, but a nurse network and booking app can be copied, and manual operations hurt margins.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Clinica Alemana and insurers partnered with Examedi rather than copying; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Pandemic demand in 2021: COVID tests made up 41 percent of home exams in Chile by August 2021, and the company said prices were up to 80 percent below traditional labs (DF).

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as 'Uber for Healthcare in Latin America' (YC page)

branding.community_and_virality: Named in Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies 2024 list per a search result; press in El Dinamo and Forbes.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is easy to say and combines exam and medical, but no distinctive brand assets were found.

pivots.from: Venture growth marketplace for home exams
pivots.why: April 2023 layoffs of about 25 percent and a 2025 recapitalization after General Catalyst exited (CEO quote on seeking profitable 50 to 60 percent growth)

outcome_analysis: Examedi grew quickly on pandemic demand, raising a $17M Series A in June 2022 led by General Catalyst, then cut 25 percent of staff in April 2023 after operations became manual and inefficient, per its CEO. Further reports describe a drop from 160 to 25 employees, founder exits and a $750K round in November 2025 as General Catalyst left, so it stalled as a venture company.
notes: Seed size conflicts: $2.7M (Contxto and Descubre.vc headlines, September 2021) vs $3.5M (Techloy). The $2.7M figure is used. Total raised per aggregators about $20.7M. Competitors: the August 2021 article on home exams named only Examedi; a low traceability third party page lists DoctorAhora, Doctor en Casa and Sami without dates, so no competitor is recorded. Ian Lee as founder comes from Chilean press, not the YC page. Layoff details (25 percent, 160 to 25 employees) come from DF and Ecosistema Startup search snippets; the later 160 to 25 date was not shown. Website not fetched separately; the YC page lists examedi.cl. Name origin not found.
